correctness.rationale: Weyl character decomposition gives squared singular values N|A_g|². Polar rank 2r hyperbolic-block normal form and k radical variables reduce quadratic graph to Q0(x)=Σ x_{2j-1}x_{2j}, up to affine automorphism. Hyperplane overlaps and bent Walsh transforms yield magnitudes M (mult K), M/2 (mult 4K(D−1)), K√D (mult KD²), including coincident levels when r=0 and r=1; summing gives rank K(D²+4D−3). Radical variables multiply ambiguity by K and repeat each nonzero value K-fold. Supported shifts have N−K values (radical differences one last coordinate, nonradical both). Generic complex reweighting makes each Fourier coefficient a nonzero polynomial, so rank=N(N−K). Independently enumerated exact Boolean Walsh ambiguity multisets through m=5 including all polar ranks; proof is all-dimensional.

limitations: Correctness of finite-dimensional Walsh formulas is not in dispute; failure is scientific novelty and distinct value.
The previous characteristic-two theorem directly covers r≥2; r=0 and 1 reductions are elementary, and generalization with radical does not create a new hard case.
